newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MBf Capital, Suria active on merger talk.
newsitem.headline: MBf Capital, Suria active on merger talk.

text.p: Malaysian financial services houses MBf Capital Bhd and Suria Capital Holdings Bhd were actively-traded on Friday on rumours of a possible merger between them, analysts and dealers said.

At the midday break, Suria Capital was up 41 cents to 3.04 ringgit with 13.22 million shares traded, and MBf Capital was 60 cents higher to 4.32 ringgit, on 9.99 million shares. They were the top two most active stocks at midday.
"There's rumours that MBF is buying Suria," said an institutional dealer with a local brokerage firm.
"We have been hearing rumours of a possible merger between MBf Capital and Suria since Wednesday," said another dealer.
Officials at both companies were not immediately available for comment.
Suria Capital owns two banking subsidiaries, Sabah Bank Bhd and the Sabah Development Bank, which are backed by the government of Sabah state in eastern Malaysia on Borneo island.

MBf Capital is a part of the MBf Holdings Bhd group of companies and is principally involved in providing financing for car and housing loans. MBf Holdings is one of Malaysia's largest property and infrastructure development groups.
MBf Holdings was the third most-active stock of the morning session, rising 17 cents to 1.44, with 7.15 million shares traded.

"There are potential synergies between the companies, as MBf Capital does not have a full banking licence, and it would like to have a foothold in Sabah," said the head of research of a local brokerage firm.
Sabah Bank currently has around 17 branches, mainly within the state, and assets of around 1.7 billion ringgit and shareholders' funds of around 200 million ringgit, the head of research said.
